## In the MRP

A backstop is a commitment by an institution whose resources the market cannot exhaust, in practice the European Central Bank or European Stability Mechanism, to buy or guarantee the debt under stated conditions; it removes the crisis equilibrium without any purchases. The state follows bright lines: clean compliance with the EU fiscal framework and a low-risk European Commission debt-sustainability classification mean eligible; an open excessive deficit procedure with effective action established means watch; non-compliance means ineligible. If eligible, the exposure probability accounts for the backstop. Upgrades out of distress through a backstop or program event require the eligible state.

## In the DAP

R6-A bright lines versus real eligibility (red flags: formal compliance with doubtful political eligibility, such as rule-of-law disputes or open conflict with EU institutions; formal ineligibility with credible political will to support). The bright lines are never overridden; the only response is monitoring, and a fragile eligible state is outlook material.

## Methods by Document Type

### [Country-Specific Recommendations](../document-types/country-specific-recommendations.qmd)

- The [Country-Specific Recommendations](../document-types/country-specific-recommendations.qmd) assess the status of the excessive deficit procedure (EDP) and the activation of the national escape clause to determine the country's standing under the EU fiscal framework. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/recommendations/Austria_2026-06-03, p. 3" aria-label="Source: ec/recommendations/Austria_2026-06-03, p. 3">ⓘ</button>
- The document confirms that the excessive deficit procedure is held in abeyance based on an assessment of effective action. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/recommendations/Belgium_2026-06-03, p. 4, p. 6" aria-label="Source: ec/recommendations/Belgium_2026-06-03, p. 4, p. 6">ⓘ</button>
- The [Country-Specific Recommendations](../document-types/country-specific-recommendations.qmd) note the activation of the national escape clause for defense spending, which permits deviations from net expenditure ceilings, and confirm that no excessive deficit procedure is open. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/recommendations/Croatia_2026-06-03, p. 3-4" aria-label="Source: ec/recommendations/Croatia_2026-06-03, p. 3-4">ⓘ</button>
- The document proposes the opening of an excessive deficit procedure due to projected non-compliance with the deficit criterion, marking a shift in fiscal status. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/recommendations/Bulgaria_2026-06-03, p. 6" aria-label="Source: ec/recommendations/Bulgaria_2026-06-03, p. 6">ⓘ</button>
- The [Country-Specific Recommendations](../document-types/country-specific-recommendations.qmd) state that the excessive deficit procedure is held in abeyance based on the [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd)’s assessment of effective action. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/recommendations/Finland_2026-06-03, p. 4" aria-label="Source: ec/recommendations/Finland_2026-06-03, p. 4">ⓘ</button>
- The [Country-Specific Recommendations](../document-types/country-specific-recommendations.qmd) reference the status of the excessive deficit procedure and the assessment of effective action, which are bright-line inputs for backstop eligibility under the EU fiscal framework. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/recommendations/France_2026-06-03, p. 4" aria-label="Source: ec/recommendations/France_2026-06-03, p. 4">ⓘ</button>
- The [Country-Specific Recommendations](../document-types/country-specific-recommendations.qmd) note that the excessive deficit procedure for [Italy](../countries/italy.qmd) is held in abeyance based on the assessment of effective action. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/recommendations/Italy_2026-06-03, p. 5" aria-label="Source: ec/recommendations/Italy_2026-06-03, p. 5">ⓘ</button>
- The [Country-Specific Recommendations](../document-types/country-specific-recommendations.qmd) conclude that the deficit criterion is fulfilled due to the national escape clause and do not propose opening an excessive deficit procedure. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/recommendations/Latvia_2026-06-03, p. 5" aria-label="Source: ec/recommendations/Latvia_2026-06-03, p. 5">ⓘ</button>
- The [Country-Specific Recommendations](../document-types/country-specific-recommendations.qmd) note that the Council has abrogated the excessive deficit decision, indicating formal closure of the procedure. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/recommendations/Malta_2026-06-03, p. 3" aria-label="Source: ec/recommendations/Malta_2026-06-03, p. 3">ⓘ</button>
- The document notes that the excessive deficit procedure for [Slovakia](../countries/slovakia.qmd) is held in abeyance following the endorsement of its fiscal-structural plan. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/recommendations/Slovakia_2026-06-03, p. 4" aria-label="Source: ec/recommendations/Slovakia_2026-06-03, p. 4">ⓘ</button>
- The assessment of excessive deficit procedure eligibility follows the EU fiscal framework (Regulation (EU) 2024/1263), considering the activation of the national escape clause and the Article 126(3) TFEU report. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/recommendations/Slovenia_2026-06-03, p. 5" aria-label="Source: ec/recommendations/Slovenia_2026-06-03, p. 5">ⓘ</button>
- Spain is subject to the preventive arm of the Stability and Growth Pact under Regulation (EU) 2024/1263. The Council endorsed its national medium-term fiscal-structural plan. Spain is not identified in the 2026 Alert Mechanism Report as requiring an in-depth review. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/recommendations/Spain_2026-06-03, p. 1-2" aria-label="Source: ec/recommendations/Spain_2026-06-03, p. 1-2">ⓘ</button>

### [Debt Sustainability Monitor](../document-types/debt-sustainability-monitor.qmd)

- The document discusses the role of the Debt Sustainability Analysis in the EU fiscal framework, including the assessment of compliance with conditions for activating the national escape clause. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 12" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 12">ⓘ</button>
- The document notes the activation of the national escape clause (NEC) for Belgium, Bulgaria, Germany, Estonia, and Greece, which deactivates specific debt sustainability safeguards. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 112, p. 113" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 112, p. 113">ⓘ</button>
- Ireland submitted a revised medium-term plan following elections, which was still being assessed at the cut-off date. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 115" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 115">ⓘ</button>

### [Post-Programme Surveillance Report](../document-types/post-programme-surveillance-report.qmd)

- The [Post-Programme Surveillance Report](../document-types/post-programme-surveillance-report.qmd) evaluates the country's capacity to service debt and assesses outstanding official loans from the European Stability Mechanism and European Financial Stability Facility as part of the broader post-programme context. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/post-programme/Post-Programme-Surveillance-Spring-2026_2026-06-03, p. 5, p. 10, p. 14, p. 18" aria-label="Source: ec/post-programme/Post-Programme-Surveillance-Spring-2026_2026-06-03, p. 5, p. 10, p. 14, p. 18">ⓘ</button>
- The assessment confirms that the country is not under an excessive deficit procedure and complies with fiscal rules, although it is monitored under the reformed Stability and Growth Pact. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/post-programme/Post-Programme-Surveillance-Spring-2026_2026-06-03, p. 8" aria-label="Source: ec/post-programme/Post-Programme-Surveillance-Spring-2026_2026-06-03, p. 8">ⓘ</button>

### [Country Report](../document-types/country-report.qmd)

- The [Country Report](../document-types/country-report.qmd) discusses [Backstop Eligibility](../parameters/backstop-eligibility.qmd) parameters by assessing compliance with EU fiscal frameworks, including the use of the national escape clause for defense spending and adherence to the medium-term fiscal-structural plan. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Bulgaria_2026-06-03, p. 6" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Bulgaria_2026-06-03, p. 6">ⓘ</button>
- The document does not explicitly assess backstop eligibility but notes that Cyprus is not in an Excessive Deficit Procedure and has compliant fiscal policies. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Cyprus_2026-06-03, p. 4" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Cyprus_2026-06-03, p. 4">ⓘ</button>
- The document does not explicitly discuss [Backstop Eligibility](../parameters/backstop-eligibility.qmd) parameters like European Stability Mechanism loans or [European Central Bank](../institutions/european-central-bank.qmd) program financing in a negative context. However, it notes that Estonia successfully synchronized its electricity grid with the EU in February 2025, a key sovereignty and stability marker. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Estonia_2026-06-03, p. 14" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Estonia_2026-06-03, p. 14">ⓘ</button>
- The assessment of backstop eligibility is informed by Belgium’s status under the Excessive Deficit Procedure and its compliance record. The report notes that the EDP is held in abeyance, but the procedure remains open, which could affect eligibility for certain support mechanisms. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Belgium_2026-06-03, p. 24" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Belgium_2026-06-03, p. 24">ⓘ</button>
- The assessment of backstop eligibility is informed by the status of the excessive deficit procedure (EDP). The EDP is open but held in abeyance due to the national escape clause for defence spending, which is a compliant deviation under the EU fiscal framework. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Finland_2026-06-03, p. 27" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Finland_2026-06-03, p. 27">ⓘ</button>
- The assessment considers France’s status under the EU fiscal framework (EDP) and compliance with recommendations. The EDP is held in abeyance, pending implementation of reforms and fiscal adjustment. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/France_2026-06-03, p. 40" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/France_2026-06-03, p. 40">ⓘ</button>
- The document references [Greece](../countries/greece.qmd)’s status under the Stability and Growth Pact, including the activation of the National Escape Clause. It mentions the in-depth review under the Macroeconomic Imbalance Procedure. Compliance with fiscal rules is assessed by the Council and the [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd). The absence of an Excessive Deficit Procedure is implicit in the discussion of the medium-term fiscal plan. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Greece_2026-06-03, p. 32, p. 36" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Greece_2026-06-03, p. 32, p. 36">ⓘ</button>
- The document references the [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd)’s assessment under the Macroeconomic Imbalance Procedure and the status of the excessive deficit procedure. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Italy_2026-06-03, p. 5, p. 40" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Italy_2026-06-03, p. 5, p. 40">ⓘ</button>
- The report notes that [Ireland](../countries/ireland.qmd) is compliant with the EU fiscal framework and there is no excessive deficit procedure open. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Ireland_2026-06-03, p. 25, p. 31" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Ireland_2026-06-03, p. 25, p. 31">ⓘ</button>
- The assessment of [Portugal](../countries/portugal.qmd) notes adherence to maximum growth rates of net expenditure recommended by the Council, with a budget surplus in 2025. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Portugal_2026-06-03, p. 34" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Portugal_2026-06-03, p. 34">ⓘ</button>

### [Economic Survey](../document-types/economic-survey.qmd)

- The OECD evaluates backstop eligibility based on the status under the EU fiscal framework, including the existence of an excessive deficit procedure and the effectiveness of corrective actions. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Austria_2026-03-19, p. 48" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Austria_2026-03-19, p. 48">ⓘ</button>
- With euro adoption, Bulgaria is now part of the European Stability Mechanism (ESM), providing additional financial protection. It is also fully integrated into the European banking framework subject to supervisory standards. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Bulgaria_2026-02-05, p. 37" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Bulgaria_2026-02-05, p. 37">ⓘ</button>
- Croatia meets both the EU debt and deficit criteria. The [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd) provided a “technical information” at the country’s request, aligning with the medium-term fiscal-structural plan. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Croatia_2026-01-30, p. 23" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Croatia_2026-01-30, p. 23">ⓘ</button>
- The perception of corruption among citizens and businesses in Croatia remains very high. This poses risks to public sector efficiency and public integrity, relevant for real eligibility assessment. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Croatia_2026-01-30, p. 35" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Croatia_2026-01-30, p. 35">ⓘ</button>
- Greece’s credit rating returned to investment grade in late 2023, making Greek sovereign bonds eligible for the [European Central Bank](../institutions/european-central-bank.qmd)’s monetary policy operations in the standard collateral framework. This upgrade reflects sustained structural reforms and enhanced banking-sector resilience. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Greece_2024-12-05, p. 21" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Greece_2024-12-05, p. 21">ⓘ</button>
- Agencies have upgraded [Italy](../countries/italy.qmd)'s sovereign debt ratings, reducing the premium on borrowing. This reflects improved fiscal management and structural reforms under the National Recovery and Resilience Plan. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Italy_2026-04-23, p. 31" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Italy_2026-04-23, p. 31">ⓘ</button>
- The European Commission’s debt-sustainability risk classification and compliance record are relevant for backstop eligibility for [Ireland](../countries/ireland.qmd), though specific status details are not explicitly detailed. The new EU fiscal rules are not currently a binding constraint for Ireland. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Ireland_2025-02-12, p. 35" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Ireland_2025-02-12, p. 35">ⓘ</button>
- Sovereign bond spreads have fallen to historically low levels relative to Germany, reflecting improved fiscal credibility. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Portugal_2026-01-06, p. 34" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Portugal_2026-01-06, p. 34">ⓘ</button>
- The [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd) assessed the 2026 Draft Budgetary Plan of [Slovenia](../countries/slovenia.qmd) as at risk of non-compliance with the maximum growth of net expenditure allowed by the fiscal plan, though within the control account threshold after using flexibility from the national escape clause. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Slovenia_2026-06-16, p. 30" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Slovenia_2026-06-16, p. 30">ⓘ</button>
- The OECD notes that the debt brake’s track record is poor. An empirical investigation found no significant stabilising response to debt levels around the introduction of the debt brake in 2012, but a stabilising response did emerge after EU accession preparations began in 2001-2003. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Slovakia_2026-06-25, p. 48-50" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Slovakia_2026-06-25, p. 48-50">ⓘ</button>

## Institutions and Data Sources

- **[European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd)**: Issued the recommendation to the Council. Assessed effective action for the excessive deficit procedure, leading to its suspension in abeyance. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/recommendations/Austria_2026-06-03, p. 2, p. 3" aria-label="Source: ec/recommendations/Austria_2026-06-03, p. 2, p. 3">ⓘ</button>
- **[Council of the EU](../institutions/council-of-the-eu.qmd)**: Adopted recommendations endorsing the national medium-term fiscal-structural plan and allowing deviations from net expenditure growth rates via the national escape clause. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/recommendations/Austria_2026-06-03, p. 3" aria-label="Source: ec/recommendations/Austria_2026-06-03, p. 3">ⓘ</button>
- **[European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd)**: Assessed the country's situation vis-à-vis the deficit criterion. Proposed the opening of an excessive deficit procedure to the Council. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/recommendations/Bulgaria_2026-06-03, p. 2-3, p. 6" aria-label="Source: ec/recommendations/Bulgaria_2026-06-03, p. 2-3, p. 6">ⓘ</button>
- **[Council of the EU](../institutions/council-of-the-eu.qmd)**: Recommended maximum growth rates of net expenditure. Adopted a Decision on the existence of an excessive deficit and a Recommendation to bring the situation to an end. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/recommendations/Bulgaria_2026-06-03, p. 4-6" aria-label="Source: ec/recommendations/Bulgaria_2026-06-03, p. 4-6">ⓘ</button>
- **[European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd)**: Issued the recommendation. Confirmed that the excessive deficit procedure is held in abeyance based on an assessment of effective action. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/recommendations/Belgium_2026-06-03, p. 3, p. 4, p. 6" aria-label="Source: ec/recommendations/Belgium_2026-06-03, p. 3, p. 4, p. 6">ⓘ</button>
- **[Council of the EU](../institutions/council-of-the-eu.qmd)**: Endorsed the national medium-term fiscal-structural plan. Allowed deviations from net expenditure limits under the national escape clause. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/recommendations/Belgium_2026-06-03, p. 3, p. 4" aria-label="Source: ec/recommendations/Belgium_2026-06-03, p. 3, p. 4">ⓘ</button>
- **[European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd)**: Issued the recommendation. Confirmed that the country is not under an excessive deficit procedure and assessed compliance with fiscal rules. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/post-programme/Post-Programme-Surveillance-Spring-2026_2026-06-03, p. 2, p. 8" aria-label="Source: ec/post-programme/Post-Programme-Surveillance-Spring-2026_2026-06-03, p. 2, p. 8">ⓘ</button>
- **[European Stability Mechanism](../institutions/european-stability-mechanism.qmd)**: Holds outstanding official loans. Staff participated in post-programme surveillance meetings. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/post-programme/Post-Programme-Surveillance-Spring-2026_2026-06-03, p. 2, p. 5, p. 10, p. 14, p. 18" aria-label="Source: ec/post-programme/Post-Programme-Surveillance-Spring-2026_2026-06-03, p. 2, p. 5, p. 10, p. 14, p. 18">ⓘ</button>
- **[European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd)**: Issued the recommendation. Confirmed that the country was not identified for an in-depth review under the Alert Mechanism Report. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/recommendations/Croatia_2026-06-03, p. 2" aria-label="Source: ec/recommendations/Croatia_2026-06-03, p. 2">ⓘ</button>
- **[Council of the EU](../institutions/council-of-the-eu.qmd)**: Endorsed the national medium-term fiscal-structural plan. Allowed the activation of the national escape clause for defense spending. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/recommendations/Croatia_2026-06-03, p. 3-4" aria-label="Source: ec/recommendations/Croatia_2026-06-03, p. 3-4">ⓘ</button>
- **[European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd)**: Issued the Country Report and assessed Croatia's implementation of Country-Specific Recommendations (CSRs). It activated the National Escape Clause for defense spending in coordination with the Council. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Croatia_2026-06-03, p. 1, p. 35, p. 42" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Croatia_2026-06-03, p. 1, p. 35, p. 42">ⓘ</button>
- **[Council of the EU](../institutions/council-of-the-eu.qmd)**: Activated the national escape clause for Bulgaria for defense spending. Endorsed Bulgaria’s medium-term fiscal-structural plan. Made financial assistance available under the Security Action for Europe (SAFE) instrument. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Bulgaria_2026-06-03, p. 6, p. 43" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Bulgaria_2026-06-03, p. 6, p. 43">ⓘ</button>
- **[Council of the EU](../institutions/council-of-the-eu.qmd)**: Activated the national escape clause for Austria for defense spending and adopted recommendations on the excessive deficit procedure. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Austria_2026-06-03, p. 6, p. 37" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Austria_2026-06-03, p. 6, p. 37">ⓘ</button>
- **[European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd)**: The European Commission assesses the implementation of country-specific recommendations (CSRs) and provides forecasts for economic and fiscal indicators. It evaluates Belgium’s progress in structural reforms and compliance with EU fiscal rules. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Belgium_2026-06-03, p. 24-29" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Belgium_2026-06-03, p. 24-29">ⓘ</button>
- **[Council of the EU](../institutions/council-of-the-eu.qmd)**: The Council of the European Union adopted a recommendation endorsing Belgium’s medium-term fiscal structural plan and a revised recommendation under Article 126(7) TFEU regarding the excessive deficit procedure. It also activated the national escape clause for defence spending. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Belgium_2026-06-03, p. 29" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Belgium_2026-06-03, p. 29">ⓘ</button>
- **[European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd)**: The issuer of the report. It provided the Spring 2026 Economic Forecast, which projects the deficit and debt trajectory. It also assessed the implementation of Country-Specific Recommendations (CSRs) and the degree of compliance with the EU fiscal framework. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Finland_2026-06-03, p. 5, p. 27-31" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Finland_2026-06-03, p. 5, p. 27-31">ⓘ</button>
- **[Council of the EU](../institutions/council-of-the-eu.qmd)**: Adopted recommendations on 21 January 2025 endorsing Finland’s medium-term fiscal-structural plan and on 8 July 2025 activating the national escape clause for defence spending. On 21 January 2026, it adopted a recommendation to correct the excessive deficit, effectively closing the EDP while holding it in abeyance. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Finland_2026-06-03, p. 4, p. 32, p. 27" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Finland_2026-06-03, p. 4, p. 32, p. 27">ⓘ</button>
- **[European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd)**: The European Commission issued this Country Report as part of the European Semester process. It assesses France’s economic, social, employment, structural, and budgetary policies. The Commission provided forecasts for GDP, deficit, and debt. It also assessed the implementation of Country-Specific Recommendations (CSRs) and the progress of the Recovery and Resilience Plan. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/France_2026-06-03, p. 1, p. 3, p. 40" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/France_2026-06-03, p. 1, p. 3, p. 40">ⓘ</button>
- **[European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd)**: The issuer of the document. It conducted the in-depth review of [Greece](../countries/greece.qmd) under the Macroeconomic Imbalance Procedure. It provides the Spring 2026 Forecast data for gross domestic product, fiscal balances, and debt. It assesses the implementation of country-specific recommendations. It manages the Recovery and Resilience Facility and Cohesion Policy funds supporting [Greece](../countries/greece.qmd). <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Greece_2026-06-03, p. 1, p. 3, p. 6, p. 36-37, p. 32-35" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Greece_2026-06-03, p. 1, p. 3, p. 6, p. 36-37, p. 32-35">ⓘ</button>
- **[European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd)**: Issued the Country Report and the In-Depth Review under the Macroeconomic Imbalance Procedure. The [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd) forecasts fiscal developments and assesses compliance with EU fiscal rules. - **[Council of the EU](../institutions/council-of-the-eu.qmd)**: The [OECD](../institutions/oecd.qmd) references the newly adopted EU fiscal rules by the [Council of the EU](../institutions/council-of-the-eu.qmd), noting that Greece’s projected debt decline ensures compliance with these rules. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Greece_2024-12-05, p. 32" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Greece_2024-12-05, p. 32">ⓘ</button>
- **[European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd)**: The [OECD](../institutions/oecd.qmd) notes that [Italy](../countries/italy.qmd)'s MTFSP aligns with commitments under the revised EU fiscal rules approved by the [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd). Revisions to the NRRP milestones were agreed with the Commission in late 2025. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Italy_2026-04-23, p. 31" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Italy_2026-04-23, p. 31">ⓘ</button>
- **[International Monetary Fund](../institutions/international-monetary-fund.qmd)**: Data from the [International Monetary Fund](../institutions/international-monetary-fund.qmd) is cited for Financial Soundness Indicators regarding banking system vulnerabilities. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Italy_2026-04-23, p. 29" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Italy_2026-04-23, p. 29">ⓘ</button>
- **[World Bank](../institutions/world-bank.qmd)**: Corruption perceptions and governance indicators are sourced from the [World Bank](../institutions/world-bank.qmd) Worldwide Governance Indicators. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Italy_2026-04-23, p. 46" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Italy_2026-04-23, p. 46">ⓘ</button>
- **[European Investment Bank](../institutions/european-investment-bank.qmd)**: The [European Investment Bank](../institutions/european-investment-bank.qmd) is mentioned in the context of public guarantee schemes and investment surveys. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Italy_2026-04-23, p. 127" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Italy_2026-04-23, p. 127">ⓘ</button>
- **[European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd)**: The survey references the European Commission’s Ageing Report for economic and budgetary projections for EU Member States from 2022 to 2070 <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Ireland_2025-02-12, p. 25" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Ireland_2025-02-12, p. 25">ⓘ</button>. It also cites the European Commission’s assessment of the draft Updated National Energy and Climate Plan of Ireland <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Ireland_2025-02-12, p. 61" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Ireland_2025-02-12, p. 61">ⓘ</button>.
- **[International Monetary Fund](../institutions/international-monetary-fund.qmd)**: The survey cites International Monetary Fund Article IV consultations and selected issues reports regarding Ireland, particularly concerning financial stability risks and non-bank financial institutions <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Ireland_2025-02-12, p. 20" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Ireland_2025-02-12, p. 20">ⓘ</button>.
- **[European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd)**: The [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd) publishes the Debt Sustainability Monitor as part of its economic surveillance duties. The document serves as input for the European Semester and the reformed EU fiscal framework. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 11, p. 12" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 11, p. 12">ⓘ</button>
- **[European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd)**: Published the Debt Sustainability Monitor 2025. Assessed the fiscal sustainability condition for activating the national escape clause (NEC) for 16 Member States. Calculated prior guidance and assessed plausibility of adjustment paths in medium-term plans. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 112" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 112">ⓘ</button>
- **[Council of the EU](../institutions/council-of-the-eu.qmd)**: Endorsed net expenditure paths for Member States. Activated the NEC based on Commission recommendations. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 112" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 112">ⓘ</button>
- **[European Central Bank](../institutions/european-central-bank.qmd)**: Participates in the Debt Sustainability Analysis (DSA) working group. Its composite indicator of systemic sovereign stress (SovCISS) is referenced in market risk charts. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 118" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 118">ⓘ</button>
- **[European Fiscal Board](../institutions/european-fiscal-board.qmd)**: Invited as an observer to the DSA working group. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 118" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 118">ⓘ</button>
- **[European Stability Mechanism](../institutions/european-stability-mechanism.qmd)**: Invited as an observer to the DSA working group. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 118" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 118">ⓘ</button>
- **[European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd)**: The [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd)'s 2024 Ageing Report provides projections for ageing-related costs, which the OECD uses to illustrate long-term fiscal pressures. The [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd) also oversees the implementation of the Recovery and Resilience Plan (RRP). <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Portugal_2026-01-06, p. 34" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Portugal_2026-01-06, p. 34">ⓘ</button>
- **[European Investment Bank](../institutions/european-investment-bank.qmd)**: The [European Investment Bank](../institutions/european-investment-bank.qmd) reports that fewer Portuguese firms are investing compared to European peers, highlighting a legacy of low investment. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Portugal_2026-01-06, p. 48" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Portugal_2026-01-06, p. 48">ⓘ</button>
- **[European Central Bank](../institutions/european-central-bank.qmd)**: The [European Central Bank](../institutions/european-central-bank.qmd)'s monetary policy easing has supported private investment. The [European Central Bank](../institutions/european-central-bank.qmd)'s data is used to track bank funding structures and non-performing loans. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Portugal_2026-01-06, p. 28" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Portugal_2026-01-06, p. 28">ⓘ</button>
- **[International Monetary Fund](../institutions/international-monetary-fund.qmd)**: The [International Monetary Fund](../institutions/international-monetary-fund.qmd)'s 2024 Article IV Consultation is cited regarding housing market risks and financial stability. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Portugal_2026-01-06, p. 31" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Portugal_2026-01-06, p. 31">ⓘ</button>
- **[Eurostat](../institutions/eurostat.qmd)**: [Eurostat](../institutions/eurostat.qmd) data is used for HICP inflation, labour force statistics, and contingent liabilities metrics. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Portugal_2026-01-06, p. 23" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Portugal_2026-01-06, p. 23">ⓘ</button>
- **[European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd)**: The [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd) assessed [Slovenia](../countries/slovenia.qmd)'s 2026 Draft Budgetary Plan as at risk of non-compliance with the EU fiscal framework but noted that deviations were within allowed flexibility margins. The Commission also confirmed the implementation status of the [Slovenia](../countries/slovenia.qmd)n Recovery and Resilience Plan. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Slovenia_2026-06-16, p. 30" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Slovenia_2026-06-16, p. 30">ⓘ</button>
- **[European Central Bank](../institutions/european-central-bank.qmd)**: The [European Central Bank](../institutions/european-central-bank.qmd) implemented a policy rate cut in June 2025, leading to decreasing interest rates on loans and deposits in [Slovenia](../countries/slovenia.qmd). The Bank of Slovenia (national central bank) adjusted macroprudential tools, such as increasing the countercyclical capital buffer. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Slovenia_2026-06-16, p. 25" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Slovenia_2026-06-16, p. 25">ⓘ</button>
- **[International Monetary Fund](../institutions/international-monetary-fund.qmd)**: The [International Monetary Fund](../institutions/international-monetary-fund.qmd) is cited regarding the assessment of active labour market policies and the fiscal impact of pension reforms. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Slovenia_2026-06-16, p. 21" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Slovenia_2026-06-16, p. 21">ⓘ</button>
- **[European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd)**: The European Commission notified a reversal of a milestone in April 2024 regarding the approval of national expenditure ceilings under the EU Recovery and Resilience Plan. The Commission also issued Country-Specific Recommendations in 2025, highlighting weaknesses in investment planning and transparency <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Slovakia_2026-06-25, p. 48, 88" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Slovakia_2026-06-25, p. 48, 88">ⓘ</button>.
- **[European Investment Bank](../institutions/european-investment-bank.qmd)**: The European Investment Bank (EIB) Investment Survey data are cited to show that lack of skilled staff is a pressing obstacle for investment in Slovakia. The EIB also notes that few companies report financing constraints as a major obstacle to investment <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Slovakia_2026-06-25, p. 82, 90" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Slovakia_2026-06-25, p. 82, 90">ⓘ</button>.
- **[International Monetary Fund](../institutions/international-monetary-fund.qmd)**: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) conducted stress tests in 2024, concluding that the Slovak banking sector possesses strong capacity to absorb shocks. The IMF’s Article IV Consultation Staff Report is also cited regarding pension reforms <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Slovakia_2026-06-25, p. 25, 30" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Slovakia_2026-06-25, p. 25, 30">ⓘ</button>.
- **[Eurostat](../institutions/eurostat.qmd)**: Eurostat data are used to track AI adoption among enterprises, showing that 18% of Slovak enterprises used AI in 2025. Eurostat also provides data on energy prices and electricity trading <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Slovakia_2026-06-25, p. 109, 134, 137" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Slovakia_2026-06-25, p. 109, 134, 137">ⓘ</button>.

| [Italy](../countries/italy.qmd) | Excessive deficit procedure held in abeyance. Sovereign debt ratings upgraded. | R6-A, Bright lines versus real eligibility: Agencies have upgraded [Italy](../countries/italy.qmd)'s sovereign debt ratings, reducing the premium on borrowing. This reflects improved fiscal management and structural reforms under the NRRP. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Italy_2026-04-23, p. 31" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Italy_2026-04-23, p. 31">ⓘ</button> |

No excessive deficit procedure. | R6-A, Bright lines versus real eligibility: The European Commission’s debt-sustainability risk classification and compliance record are relevant. The new EU fiscal rules are not currently a binding constraint for Ireland. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Ireland_2025-02-12, p. 35" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Ireland_2025-02-12, p. 35">ⓘ</button> |
